Defamation on the Internet in Italy: How to Get Defamatory Content Removed

By RMA — Web Reputation Agency

Online defamation in Italy is a criminal offence under article 595 of the Criminal Code, treated as aggravated when it is committed through the internet, and it can be tackled on three fronts at once: a criminal complaint, a civil claim for damages and the removal of the content itself. Effective online defamation removal depends above all on speed, because the deadline for a complaint is three months and digital evidence can vanish within hours.

What counts as defamation on the internet under Italian law

Defamation (diffamazione) means damaging another person's reputation while communicating with several people in that person's absence. A post on a public profile, a forum thread, a review or a blog article automatically reaches an indeterminate audience, so the "several people" requirement is practically always met online. Article 595, paragraph 3, raises the penalty when the offence is committed by the press or by "any other means of publicity", and Italian case law consistently places websites and social networks in that category.

For a statement to be defamatory, Italian courts look for a combination of elements:

  • the victim is identifiable, even without being named, through a nickname, a photo, the business address or context that readers recognise;
  • the content is objectively offensive to honour or reputation, not merely unpleasant;
  • the message was accessible to more than one person other than the victim;
  • the author acted with awareness of the offensive meaning (general intent is enough, no specific aim to harm is required).

Where defamation ends

An insult sent privately to the victim alone is no longer a crime in Italy: insult (ingiuria) was decriminalised in 2016 and today only gives rise to a civil penalty. Equally, true facts of public interest reported in a measured tone, and harsh but relevant opinions, fall under the rights of reporting and criticism. A one-star review saying the service was slow is criticism; a review accusing a named owner of fraud without any basis is a very different matter.

How to collect evidence that will hold up

Preserve the content before reporting it or contacting anyone, because a report often prompts the author to delete the post and the platform to remove it without keeping a copy you can access. A simple screenshot is admissible, yet it is easy to contest; prosecutors and judges in Milan, Rome and elsewhere give far more weight to evidence whose integrity can be demonstrated.

  1. Record the full URL, date and time of viewing, and the author's profile link, not just the text.
  2. Capture comments, shares and reactions, since they prove the spread of the content and can identify further offenders.
  3. Obtain a certified acquisition: a forensic capture with hash values and timestamps made by a technical consultant, or a report drawn up by a notary.
  4. List witnesses who saw the content and clients or partners who mentioned it to you.
  5. Keep a log of every later repost or copy, with the same level of detail.

The criminal complaint: deadline, venue and the role of Polizia Postale

A complaint (querela) must be filed within three months of the day the victim learned of the defamatory content, under article 124 of the Criminal Code. It can be lodged with the Polizia Postale e delle Comunicazioni, the Carabinieri, any police station or directly with the Public Prosecutor's office, preferably drafted by a lawyer and accompanied by the evidence described above.

The aggravated offence under paragraph 3 of article 595 carries imprisonment from six months to three years or a fine; attributing a specific fact (for example, a precise episode of cheating customers) aggravates the position further. Polizia Postale is particularly useful when the author hides behind a fake profile, as it can request identification data from platforms and providers through the prosecutor, including from operators based abroad.

Seizure and the leverage of the complaint

During the investigation the prosecutor may ask the judge for a preventive seizure of the web page, carried out by blocking access to it, subject to the special protections that apply to registered news outlets. The complaint can also be withdrawn (remissione di querela) if the author removes the content and compensates the victim, which often makes it a practical negotiating tool rather than an end in itself.

Civil damages and urgent court orders

Compensation can be claimed either by joining the criminal proceedings as a civil party (parte civile) or through a separate civil action under articles 2043 and 2059 of the Civil Code. The civil route is also available when the complaint deadline has passed, with a much longer limitation period.

When the content is causing ongoing harm, an urgent order under article 700 of the Code of Civil Procedure can require the author or the site manager to remove it within weeks rather than years. The table below compares the main legal routes available in Italy.

RouteWhat it achievesWhen it makes sense
Querela (criminal)Investigation, identification of anonymous authors, possible conviction and seizureSerious accusations, anonymous attackers, within three months
Civil actionDamages for economic and non-economic harmMeasurable losses: cancelled contracts, lost bookings, reputational cost
Urgent order (art. 700 c.p.c.)Fast court-ordered removalContent spreading quickly and causing immediate damage

Damages are awarded on evidence, so keep proof of commercial impact such as lost tenders or emails from clients citing the post.

How to remove defamatory content from platforms and Google

Legal proceedings do not delete anything by themselves, so the request to remove defamatory content should run in parallel with any complaint. Platforms are the fastest route: under the Digital Services Act, hosting services must offer a notice-and-action mechanism, assess notices of illegal content diligently and give a reasoned decision, as explained in our article on platform liability after the Digital Services Act.

A well-built notice identifies the exact URL, quotes the statements, explains why they are false or defamatory under Italian law and attaches proof. In practice, internet defamation removal works through several channels:

  • the platform's own reporting flow for harassment, false information or defamation;
  • a formal DSA notice to the host or social network, which creates a documented duty to act;
  • a letter from a lawyer to the site owner or editor demanding removal and, where relevant, a correction;
  • Google's legal removal request for defamation, which can delist the URL from search results in Europe even when the page itself stays online.

Delisting and deletion are not the same outcome, and choosing the wrong one wastes time; our guide to removal, deindexing and ranking suppression explains the differences.

Combining the routes without amplifying the damage

The most effective sequence is to preserve evidence first, send removal notices next, file the complaint within three months and decide on a civil claim once the harm can be quantified. Running everything at once without a plan can backfire: a public legal threat posted in reply to a review frequently attracts more attention than the review itself.

Online defamation removal is rarely a single action. Evidence, platform notices, the querela and the civil claim each solve a different part of the problem, and timing decides which ones remain available.

Businesses should also distinguish a real defamatory attack from an unfair but lawful negative opinion. In the second case a calm public reply, following the approach in our article on responding to a negative review, often protects the brand better than litigation.
